_about: Defaults of the AutoCAD -> Archicad site tool. The drawing and the point cloud are the only inputs needed: everything else is worked out (auto) or optional. To keep values for a project, put them in config/project.json (same layout, only the keys that change); any value can also be set on the command line (--set section.key=value). Keys starting with '_' are notes.

paths._output_dir: where the results go, relative to the folder the command is run from (or a full path)
paths._work_dir: cache of intermediate results (safe to delete); null = %LOCALAPPDATA%/ing_studio_toolkit/autocad_to_archicad
paths._point_cloud: survey point cloud of the site (needed; also the second file on the command line): its terrain becomes the mesh (the cloud itself is not put into the PLN)
paths._relief_tool: the relief tool that turns the point cloud into a terrain model; null = the pointcloud_to_archicad_relief folder next to this tool
paths._relief_work_dir: its cache folder; null = its default (%LOCALAPPDATA%/ing_studio_toolkit/pointcloud_to_archicad_relief)

tools._note: null = found automatically in the standard install folders

read._note: DWG files are read through AutoCAD's own console (no window): AutoCAD Architecture/Civil objects are turned into plain AutoCAD objects first, then the drawing is saved as DXF

drawing._units: auto | mm | cm | m | in | ft: what one drawing unit is. auto = the DWG setting, and when that is missing a guess from the size of the drawing (checked again when it is matched to the map)
drawing._region: auto = the site plan is found automatically (the largest drawing in model space) | [x1, y1, x2, y2] in drawing units
drawing._region_gap_m: drawings further apart than this are separate regions
drawing._text_encoding: auto = texts and layer names written with old Armenian fonts (ARMSCII-8) are turned into real Armenian letters | none

layers._note: what each drawing layer holds. auto = worked out from the geometry: existing buildings = the outlines that match OpenStreetMap's buildings; new streets = a hatch layer with axis lines along the middle of its strips, and the hatches lining it (sidewalks); kerbs = lines on both sides of OpenStreetMap's streets; new buildings = the outlines that cast the drawn shadows (a footprint slid in one direction); trees = layers of round symbols. Or a list of layer name patterns (case-insensitive, * = anything), e.g. ["*ROADS*"]
layers._hints: words in layer names that order the candidates and break ties (the geometry decides)

documents._note: OPTIONAL project PDFs (--doc FILE) read as data (no AI): sheet texts, '<levels> <area> SQM' statements, area tables (area by function) and the areas outlined in colour on level plans, which are placed on the drawing. Without them there are no underground levels and no programme checks
documents._files: PDF files (paths relative to where the command is run); also --doc FILE
documents._scale: auto = a '1 : N' text on the sheets, else from the sheets' own stated areas against the outlined areas | a number N (1:N)
documents._mark_rgb: colour of the outline that marks an area on a level plan (red, green, blue 0-255), and how far a pixel may differ
documents._level_prefixes: letters of level names in the statements (B1, B2 ...)
documents._read_total_outlines: also read outlines of sheets that state an area without levels (a total)
documents._below_ground_functions: table rows (name starts with) that are below ground, the rest is above-ground floor area
documents._parking_rules: parking demand of the programme rows (name patterns): ՀՀՇՆ 30-01-2023 Table 56 (m2 of floor area per space), flats as units of unit_m2 with 0.8-1 space each (Table 8, note 12); used by the report

*HOTEL*.note: by the hotel's class (Table 56 refers to the hotel norms) - not counted

documents._min_within_1m_pct: a plan is placed on the drawing only when this share of its lines falls within 1 m of the drawing's lines, and min_lift_pct more than when the page is turned away

site._lonlat: auto = where the names of the input files (and the drawing's texts) point, checked by the building match | [longitude, latitude] of a point within a few hundred metres of the site (--lonlat)
site._geocode_api: OpenStreetMap's gazetteer, for the place names (at most one request a second)
site._osm_margin_m: OpenStreetMap data is fetched this far around the drawing

georef._note: the drawing is placed on the map by matching its building outlines (layers.existing_buildings) to the OpenStreetMap buildings (rotation and shift; scale 1)
georef._mode: auto | manual (then manual_rotation_deg and manual_origin_utm are used)
georef._search_radius_m: how far the real position may be from a given site.lonlat; for a place found from a name, windows of this radius cover the whole site plan
georef._max_places: candidate places (from the place names) tried, best first
georef._max_layer_tries: layers with building-like shapes tried at each place, most likely first
georef._min_peak_ratio: the best match must score at least this many times the typical score, else the run stops (set georef.mode=manual)
georef._manual_origin_utm: [easting, northing] of the drawing point 0,0 (manual mode)

cloud._note: the point cloud terrain is placed on the drawing by matching the gaps buildings leave in the ground points to the drawing's building outlines
cloud._mode: auto | manual (then manual_rotation_deg and manual_origin_dwg_m are used)
cloud._manual_origin_dwg_m: [x, y] in drawing metres of the point cloud point 0,0 (manual mode)
cloud._z_to_altitude: metres added to point cloud heights to get altitudes above sea level: auto = from the open world terrain model below (SRTM-based, about +-3 m), or a number (from a surveyed benchmark)
cloud._world_terrain_url: open world terrain tiles (AWS Terrain Tiles, GeoTIFF, Web Mercator) used for the altitude of the point cloud

terrain._resolution_m: grid of the terrain model in drawing coordinates
terrain._note: ONE terrain mesh inside the point cloud footprint: adaptive points of the (road-adjusted) terrain, a point grid under the paving and lines along its edges

roads._standards: street classes of ՀՀՇՆ 30-01-2023 Table 29 (Armenia, in force since 30 May 2023; replaced ՀՀՇՆ 30-01-2014 / SNiP 2.07.01-89): design speed km/h on [normal, rugged, mountainous] terrain, lane width m, lanes, smallest sidewalk m
roads._design_speeds: by design speed km/h: smallest horizontal radius m, largest grade per mille (exceptional grade allowed on stretches up to exceptional_max_length_m), smallest crest / sag vertical radius m, sight distance m

40.source: SNiP 2.05.02-85 Table 10, which ՀՀՇՆ 32-01-2022 continues (check against ՀՀՇՆ 32-01-2022)

roads._terrain: terrain category of the site for the design speed: auto | normal | rugged | mountainous (auto = the tool's rule of thumb from the median ground slope under the new streets, per mille)
roads._checks: further checks of ՀՀՇՆ 30-01-2023 (reported): kerb radius at junctions (12 m; 6 m in constrained / rebuilt places), turning place at a dead end (15 m across), sidewalks for wheelchairs (at most 83 per mille = 1:12; above 30 per mille a 5 m level landing every 100 m)
roads._profile: longitudinal profile rules: min grade for drainage (checked, reported), tighter grade limit in serpentine bends, cross slopes, kerb; the vertical curves come from the design speed

profile._serpentine: bends tighter than serpentine_radius_m are serpentines: grade at most serpentine_max_grade_permille, radius at least serpentine_min_radius_m (SNiP 2.05.02-85 serpentines at 20 km/h; ՀՀՇՆ 30-01-2023 Table 33 allows 15 m at 20 km/h, 12 m at 15 km/h on ramps)
profile._exceptional_grade_cost: the design may use the exceptional grade (e.g. 120 per mille at 30 km/h) where that saves at least this much height difference to the ground (m2) per metre and per mille over the normal limit; stretches longer than allowed are reported. null = never
profile._pavement_m: thickness of the paving: the street bodies are this thick and lie on the terrain, which runs this far below a carriageway's surface (kerb + this below a sidewalk's)
profile._junction_blend_m: where streets meet, a point's height blends the streets' surfaces, each weighted by exp(-(its distance - the nearest one's) / this): smooth junctions, and the legs of a serpentine stay apart
profile._surface_smoothing_m: the street surfaces are smoothed over this distance (no steps at junctions and tight bends; the kerb stays sharp)
profile._tie_in_weight: how strongly a street end is pulled to the height of the existing street it joins (per metre of mismatch; the ground pulls with about 5 per metre of street). The rules always win: a mismatch is reported

existing._note: existing streets come from OpenStreetMap (not tunnels or covered passages), are moved and widened to the kerb lines of the drawing (layers.kerbs) where it has them, and get a clean surface on the terrain; they stop at buildings
existing._osm_classes: OpenStreetMap road types taken, with the carriageway width used when neither the drawing nor OSM (width/lanes) says
existing._edge_blend_m: the ground beside an existing street is eased onto its edge within this distance (at most the side slopes of roads.earthworks; no walls)
existing._regrade_grade_permille: where a new street cannot join an existing one at its height within the rules, the existing street is regraded locally, the change tapering off at this grade (reported). null = leave it and report the step

proposed._note: proposed streets come from the drawing: carriageway areas (layers.carriageway), their axis lines (layers.axes; none = centre lines computed from the carriageway) and sidewalk areas (layers.sidewalks); the profile is designed to the rules above. Their surfaces stop at buildings
proposed._class: street class of the new streets (a key of roads.standards)
proposed._sidewalk_band_m: of the drawing's sidewalk areas only this band along the kerb is treated as street sidewalk (raised by the kerb, set to the street); wider paved areas such as plazas and terraces are left to the architecture
proposed._sidewalks: when the drawing has no sidewalk areas: add sidewalks along the new streets (width from the class)
proposed._snap_m: axis line ends this close to another axis line are joined to it
proposed._ends_join_existing_m: a street end this close to an existing street is tied to its height
proposed._prune_m: centre line branches shorter than this (corners of the area) are dropped

earthworks._note: the terrain is cut / filled around the new streets with these slopes (horizontal : vertical); where the slope would run further than max_daylight_m a retaining wall is needed and reported
earthworks._segment_m: street stretch length whose side slopes are computed together (short enough that the legs of a serpentine are separate)
earthworks._max_fill_m: a new street standing higher than this above the ground is a bridge / viaduct: the ground stays as it is under it (no embankment; reported). null = always an embankment
earthworks._bridge_deck_m: thickness of a bridge deck body
earthworks._walls: retaining walls are modelled as pieces about wall_segment_m long, wall_thickness_m thick, their footing wall_footing_m below the lower side

buildings._note: 3D buildings, trees and underground levels (layers: see the layers section). Existing buildings: heights from OpenStreetMap. Proposed buildings: storeys read from the drawn shadows (a building's shadow = its footprint slid by a length that grows with its height). Underground levels: the level outlines of the project documents (when given). The streets and the earthworks leave the ground under the buildings as it is
buildings._storey_m: storey heights: height = ground storey + (storeys - 1) x storey
buildings._existing_default_storeys: existing buildings whose height OSM does not know
buildings._courtyard_shared: an outline face OSM does not know, whose outline runs along other faces for this share, is a courtyard (left out)
buildings._shadow_per_storey_m: auto = the largest step that makes the drawn shadow lengths whole multiples | a length in m
buildings._proposed_default_storeys: proposed buildings without a drawn shadow
buildings._joined_shared: a proposed face without a shadow of its own takes the storeys of a shadowed face it shares at least this share of one side with (a tower drawn in parts)
buildings._demolish: an existing building is to be demolished (left out, listed) when the new buildings, carriageways or sidewalks cover this share of its footprint, or this many m2 of it; smaller overlaps are drawing tolerances: the street stops at the building
buildings._embed_m: bodies reach this far below the lowest terrain under them and around them (no gaps on slopes and next to cut streets)
buildings._tree_min_height_m: trees are at least this high; a tree standing on a carriageway is left out
buildings._checks: ՀՀՇՆ 30-01-2023 checks of the new buildings of at least min_storeys (reported): gaps between them (10 m between long sides with windows; 6 m fire distance between I-II fire-resistance buildings, Table 50), and at most 25 m from a street (else a 6 m fire lane; checked by the roads stage)

underground._note: levels read from the project documents (B1, B2 ...), stacked down from the ground floor
underground._ground_level: auto = the highest terrain over the top level's outline | altitude in m

archicad._note: <drawing>_FromDWG.pln starts as a copy of the Archicad template. Everything on layers starting with the prefixes below is replaced on every write. The terrain is a mesh; streets, sidewalks, walls and buildings are Morph solids with the surfaces below; trees are library objects
archicad._z_reference: auto = project zero at a round altitude just below the site (10 m steps) | a number (m above sea level)
archicad._favorite_terrain: Archicad favourite the terrain mesh is based on (its surface)
archicad._road_cell_m: the street bodies are triangulated on a grid this fine (they follow the profile and the cross fall); the terrain mesh has a point at each grid corner under the paving
archicad._paving_edge_gap_m: a terrain line this far outside the paving's edge lifts the ground flush with the paving's top
archicad._surfaces: surfaces made in the PLN (name, colour red / green / blue 0-1) and what uses them
archicad._tree_objects: library parts used for the trees, the first one the project's library has; sized to the crown and height
archicad._two_d: copy the drawing (site plan region) as 2D lines, fills and texts onto layers 'DWG - <layer>'
archicad._text_scale: drawing scale used to turn text heights into Archicad paper sizes (mm)
